 (St. Paul) - A defendant acquitted in the first Feeding Our Future trial is headed to federal prison for trying to bribe a juror. 44-year-old Said Farah was sentenced Friday in St. Paul to six-and-a-half years behind bars for his role in a scheme that offered a juror $120,000 in cash to vote for acquittal. The juror immediately reported the bribe to authorities. Federal Judge Eric Tostrud praised the juror’s actions, calling her a hero and saying jury bribery threatens the integrity of the justice system.
